text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 12 in history.

100 BC - Gaius Julius Caesar, Roman general, statesman and dictator was born. After a string of victories in Gaul, Egypt and Africa, he was made dictator for life and Consul for 10 years. He was assassinated on 15 March 44 BC.
1191 - In the Third Crusade, Richard the Lionheart took the city of Acre.
1543 - Henry VIII of England married his sixth and final wife, Catherine Parr, widow of Lord Latimer, at Hampton Court Palace.

1691 - William III with English forces under Godert de Ginkel defeated James II with allied armies of the French and Irish at the decisive Battle of Aughrim. At least 6,000 soldiers were killed by the English.
1817 - Henry David Thoreau, U.S. writer and student of nature, was born. He was known as the "hermit of Walden" because he lived in the woods around Walden pond for several years.
1854 - U.S. inventor and industrialist George Eastman was born; he founded Eastman Kodak which for years held a virtual monopoly in the camera and film industry.
1884 - Amedeo Modigliani, Italian painter of the modern school, born.
1895 - Norwegian soprano Kirsten Flagstad, famed for her performances of Wagner and noted for her noble and easy delivery, born.
1895 - Oscar Hammerstein II born. Known for his collaboration with Richard Rodgers, he was a lyricist and the librettist of "The Desert Song", "South Pacific", the "Sound of Music" and many others.
1906 - Alfred Dreyfus, French artillery officer who was falsely accused of treason, was finally pardoned and restored to his rank and regiment.
1910 - Charles Stewart Rolls, aviator and co-founder of Rolls-Royce, became Britain's first aviation victim when he crashed his Wright biplane near Bournemouth.
1920 - The Panama Canal was formally opened, six years after the first ship sailed through it.
1941 - An armistice was signed which ended the fighting in Syria between the allies and the Vichy French.
1941 - An Anglo-Soviet agreement was signed in Moscow for mutual assistance against Hitler's Germany.
1970 - China agreed to make an extensive loan to Tanzania and Zambia to build the Tanzam railway.
1979 - After 80 years of British rule, Kiribati, formerly the Gilbert Islands, achieved independence.
1996 - Britain's Prince Charles and Princess Diana agreed the terms of their divorce, ending a 15-year marriage.
1996 - The European Court of Justice rejected a demand by Britain for the immediate suspension of the European Union's worldwide ban on British beef exports.
1996 - Former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi was charged with illegal political party funding and ordered to stand trial along with ex-premier Bettino Craxi.
